bitsWins: Live, graded practice with zero setup: the learner's prompt runs on Claude and a Claude judge marks it, free and with no API key. Anthropic, DLAI, HF, Microsoft and Kaggle all need a key, a notebook or an account setup; Scrimba is interactive but paid and ungraded.
Lesson size: 5-8 minutes, one idea. Every major free rival runs 1-20 hours per course.
Two reading depths in one lesson; no competitor adapts the text to the reader.
Claude-first and current; the official free alternatives in Python lag on TypeScript and the edge.
TypeScript + Cloudflare edge as the deployment story; only Cloudflare's own docs and one freeCodeCamp handbook cover it, neither as a course.
mustImprove: Breadth and brand: Anthropic now gives away 20+ hours of official Claude courses with certificates. We cannot out-official them, so every lesson must be shorter, more hands-on and better graded.
MCP: we only teach using a server. Six free courses teach building one; we need a remote, TypeScript, Workers-hosted MCP course on the current SDK (createMcpHandler, Streamable HTTP, OAuth).
Evals: Kaggle, OpenAI Academy, DLAI, Maven ($4,400) and Anthropic all teach evaluation. We have no evals course.
Proof of build: Cloudflare guides, the HF MCP course and Kaggle end in a deployed thing. Our code courses end in reading about a deploy; nothing checks the learner's own Worker.
Freshness discipline: Cloudflare rewrote its Agents quick start on Oct 29, 2026 and deprecated McpAgent. Code lessons need pinned versions, a verified-on date and a CI job that re-runs the tutorial.

Coding-agent workflow (skills, subagents, hooks, AGENTS.md) is now taught free by Anthropic, DLAI, HF Context Course and AI Hero. Our frontend-with-agents course must ship a graded real UI, not repeat skills theory.
Video and community: rivals have video, Discord and live events. We have little video and no community.

recommendations.title: Make the Cloudflare build one repo with checkpoints and a grader
recommendations.why: No free course takes a learner from npm create to a deployed Claude agent and then checks it. Give each lesson a git tag and a small check (a CLI or an endpoint bits calls on the learner's workers.dev URL) that marks the step done. This is the one thing Cloudflare's docs, Scrimba and Frontend Masters don't do.

recommendations.title: Pin versions and run the tutorial in CI weekly
recommendations.why: Cloudflare rewrote the Agents quick start on Oct 29, 2026 and deprecated McpAgent. Every code lesson should state package versions and a verified-on date, and a scheduled job should scaffold the tutorial against the latest agents and wrangler releases and fail loudly when it breaks.

recommendations.title: Audit ship-an-agent-to-the-edge against the current Agents SDK before building on it
recommendations.why: It uses Agent, getAgentByName and this.sql. The Agent class still exists, but the docs now explain it through a Lifecycle and .use() capabilities. Check the details and the intro framing so the new tutorials don't start from a stale base.

recommendations.title: MCP course: remote-first, TypeScript, on Workers
recommendations.why: The field is crowded but local and Python-heavy (Anthropic, DLAI, HF). Teach createMcpHandler, Streamable HTTP, OAuth, testing with MCP Inspector and Claude, and MCP security (tool poisoning, confused deputy, scoped tokens). Grade it by connecting to the learner's deployed server and calling a tool.

recommendations.title: Claude by default, through AI Gateway, with one Workers AI swap lesson
recommendations.why: Cloudflare's examples default to Workers AI or OpenAI. A Claude-first Cloudflare path is our niche. One lesson showing the provider swap keeps it honest and cheap for learners.

recommendations.title: Add a short evals course on the coach and judge we already run
recommendations.why: Every serious rival teaches evals and Maven charges $4,400 for it. We already have a rubric judge in production: let learners write test cases and a rubric, then see their judge agree or disagree with ours.

recommendations.title: Frontend-with-agents: ship a real UI, graded on the deployed page
recommendations.why: Skills and subagents theory is free from Anthropic, DLAI and HF. Our angle: build and deploy a front end with Claude Code plus a skill, then grade the live page (axe, a screenshot rubric, a test). Link Anthropic's skills and subagents courses for the theory.

recommendations.title: Lead with 'try a graded prompt in 30 seconds, no key'
recommendations.why: It's the one thing no free rival offers. Put a live exercise on the landing page and on course pages for signed-out visitors, so the difference shows before anyone reads a syllabus.

recommendations.title: Mark phone lessons and desk lessons
recommendations.why: On-the-go is our audience, but building on Cloudflare needs a laptop. Label each lesson so a learner can do concepts and checks on a phone and the build steps at a desk, and resume the build from where the phone left off.

recommendations.title: Certificates that link to proof of work
recommendations.why: HF and Kaggle certificates drive huge sign-ups. Ours can be stronger: a certificate that links to the learner's deployed agent or MCP server, checked by bits.

recommendations.title: A coding-agent workflow mini-course
recommendations.why: AI Hero, HF and Anthropic show strong demand (AGENTS.md, hooks, plan, test, review). Five lessons with graded exercises fill our biggest topic gap and lead into the frontend course.

recommendations.title: Curate 'Down the rabbit hole' from this list
recommendations.why: Link the long-form official courses (Claude Academy, DLAI MCP, Cloudflare docs, Karpathy) instead of rewriting them. It makes bits the fast front door and costs little.
